title: Increasing or decreasing
text: A "one-to-one" function must assign a unique output to every unique input. What happens to the outputs as you move from $$x=0$$ toward the endpoints?
choices: $$\cos(x)$$ decreases toward both $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$ and $$x=\frac{-\pi}{2}$$, so $$\cos(x)$$ fails the horizontal line test as there is a peak at $$x=0$$
$$\cos(x)$$ increases toward both $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$ and $$x=\frac{-\pi}{2}$$, so $$\cos(x)$$ fails the horizontal line test as there is a valley at $$x=0$$
\n$$\cos(x)$$ decreases toward $$x=\frac{-\pi}{2}$$ and increases toward $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$, so outputs are all unique
$$\cos(x)$$ increases toward $$x=\frac{-\pi}{2}$$ and decreases toward $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$, so outputs are all unique

title: Test midpoints and end points
text: Calculate $$\cos(-\pi/2)$$ and $$\cos(\pi/2).$$ If these values are identical, the function has "doubled back" on itself.

title: Graph the function
text: The function increases from $$x=\frac{-\pi}{2}$$ up to $$x=0$$, then decreases to $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$, meaning it doubles back through the same output values.\n##figure1.gif##
